catalog_quote: The phonology of the languages of the Tirio Family is relatively complex. The results of a superficial phonological study are still tentative, but they seem to possess the following consonant phonemes: [...] The bracketed phonemes are doubtful. The vowel phonemes appear to be: a æ e i o u œ ə. Vowel length is phonemic. Several diphthongs occur. Stress appears to be phonemic, and a complex rhythm system is present. No tonal system has been observed. The syllable structure is comparatively simple and open syllables consisting of C+V or C+V+V are overwhelmingly predominant initially and medially.

The results of a superficial phonological study are still tentative, but they seem to possess the following consonant phonemes: [consonant table].. The vowel phonemes appear to be: a æ e i o u œ ə. Vowel length is phonemic. Several diphthongs occur. Stress appears to be phonemic, and a complex rhythm system is present. No ton…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Wurm reports, for the Tirio family as a whole (Tirio/Baramu, Aturu, Lewada-Dewara, Mutum), that stress is (tentatively) phonemic, i.e. contrastive and not fixed by rule, with a complex rhythm system and no tone. He gives no placement rule and no Were-specific data; the reading 'lexical (unpredictable)' is only what 'phonemic' implies.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed; only 'a complex rhythm system is present'.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the whole passage is hedged ('appears to be', 'superficial phonological study.. still tentative').
new_statements.domain_note: Family-level typological summary, not a description of Were; based on Wurm's own field wordlists of the Tirio Family (materials collected by Capell, Gore, Hoel and Wurm). Word vs phrase not distinguished; no citation forms given. Wurm 1975: 331 repeats at stock level that all Trans-Fly languages share 'a complex stress system with rhythm principles' and (p. 335) that the two-tone system of Kiwaian/Eastern Trans-Fly 'appears to be absent from the languages of the Tirio Family'.
new_statements.identity_note: The only stress statement found is family-level: Wurm 1971 describes 'the languages of the Tirio Family' (Tirio = Baramu [bmz], Aturu = Makayam [aup], Lewada-Dewara, Mutum = Bitur [mcc]) collectively, not Were. Wurm's 'Lewada-Dewara' dialect group (pp. 142-143) comprises Lewada and Balamula villages on the Fly (Makayam [aup]) plus Dewala village on Sumogi Island, which per Wurm absorbed the Tagota and Weridai populations (Williams 1936) and which is the home of Were/Kiunum [wei] (ISO CR 2010-004; Jore & Alemán 2002 'Were of Dewala', only 47% lexical similarity with Lewada/Aduru per Usher's table). Glottolog maps Wurm's Lewada-Dewara to Makayam [aup]; Wikipedia/Evans 2018 map Lewada-Dewara to Were; so the statement covers Were only insofar as it covers the whole family. No Were-specific phonology exists in Glottolog 5.3, OLAC (Dec 2024), SIL's archive or the Newguineaworld source inventory.

sources.note: Section 3.32.3 (p. 144), typological notes on the Tirio Family (Tirio, Aturu, Lewada-Dewara, Mutum) from Wurm's own 'superficial phonological study': 'Stress appears to be phonemic, and a complex rhythm system is present. No tonal system has been observed.' No placement rule; family-level, not Were-specific. pp. 142-143 place Dewala village (= Were/Kiunum) inside his Lewada-Dewara dialect group together with Lewada and Balamula (Makayam).

sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A. 1975. The Trans-Fly (sub-phylum-level) stock. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, Vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 323-344. Canberra: ANU.http://hdl.handle.net/1885/252966
sources.note: Stock-level only: p. 331 'On the phonological level, they all share a suprasegmental system which manifests itself in a complex stress system with rhythm principles, and in addition, the languages of the Kiwaian and Eastern Trans-Fly Families seem to possess a two-tone system with usually low to very low functional load.' p. 335: the two-tone system 'appears to be absent from the languages of the Tirio Family.' Lists Lewada-Dewara (450 speakers) under the Tirio Family, p. 328. No placement rule.
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study, Vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38)

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. Lower Fly River. Newguineaworld (UZH mirror).https://newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch/families/trans-new-guinea/fly-river/lower-fly-river/start
sources.note: Comparative reconstruction only; posits 'a final destressed archiphonemic vowel' *ə in Proto-Lower Fly River but says nothing about stress placement in Were. Its source inventory for Were is exhaustive and short: Williams 1936 (7 terms for Arama), Jore 2002 (190-term wordlist, Dewala village), Jore & Alemán 2002: 43-48 (162 comparative terms). The dedicated 'Were' page is an empty stub.
No phonology; cites only Ethnologue and UN village coordinates; notes Were = Weredai = Kiunum, Dewara village, and that Evans (2018) calls it Lewada-Dewara (700 speakers).
